title: Exploring the Potential for Large Language Models to Demonstrate Rational Probabilistic Beliefs
abstract: Advances in the general capabilities of large language models (LLMs) have led to their use for information retrieval, and as components in automated decision systems. A faithful representation of probabilistic reasoning in these models may be essential to ensure trustworthy, explainable and effective performance in these tasks. Despite previous work suggesting that LLMs can perform complex reasoning and well-calibrated uncertainty quantification, we find that current versions of this class of model lack the ability to provide rational and coherent representations of probabilistic beliefs. To demonstrate this, we introduce a novel dataset of claims with indeterminate truth values and apply a number of well-established techniques for uncertainty quantification to measure the ability of LLM's to adhere to fundamental properties of probabilistic reasoning.

claims.text: Current state-of-the-art LLMs frequently violate basic principles of probabilistic reasoning such as complementarity and monotonicity.
Larger closed-source LLMs achieve higher accuracy on monotonicity evaluation tasks than smaller open-source models.
When larger LLMs produce incorrect monotonic probability estimations, the magnitude of their deviation from correct bounds is larger than that of smaller models like Gemma.
Chain-of-thought prompting provides performance gains on monotonicity tasks for smaller models but yields only marginal gains for larger models.
The Argumentative LLM (ArgLLM) technique achieves equal or higher accuracy than chain-of-thought prompting on monotonicity generalisation tasks for closed-source models.
Top-K logit sampling increases monotonicity specialisation accuracy for GPT-4o compared to direct prompting.

limitations.text: Top-K Logit Sampling could not be applied to smaller open-source models because they failed to consistently adhere to numerical output formatting instructions.
The ArgLLM method is computationally expensive as it requires generating multiple layers of arguments and confidence assignments for every claim.
Evaluation of GPT-4o was restricted to a reduced sample size of 100 claim pairs due to API usage costs.
Direct prompting-based methods are insufficient to ascertain the internal uncertainty of LLM outputs.

future_work.text: Investigating neurosymbolic approaches that combine LLMs with symbolic probabilistic reasoning modules to enforce logical probabilistic constraints.

methodologies.name: Rational Probabilistic Belief (RPB) evaluation framework
methodologies.description: Evaluation of LLM adherence to probabilistic axioms of complementarity and monotonicity across synthetically generated claim variations using multiple uncertainty quantification techniques.
